program_name: Economics — Italian official denomination: "Economics - Scienze economiche" (English denomination used by the University: "Economics"). Second-cycle (Laurea Magistrale) degree, 2 years, 120 ECTS, with two curricula: "Economics" and "Sustainable Development".
level: master (second-cycle degree / Laurea Magistrale / Corso di Laurea Magistrale, 2 years, 120 ECTS)
teaching_language: English — fully English-taught. The 2026/27 Economia Manifesto degli studi states for this course "Corso erogato in inglese" and, in the course-specific section, "Gli insegnamenti di entrambi i curricula sono erogati in lingua inglese" (the courses of both curricula are delivered in English). The programme is also listed by UNIUD among the "Degrees taught entirely in English" and in the 2026/2027 Additional Notice under "List of Master's degree courses taught entirely in English". No Italian-language track or Italian-taught curriculum exists for this LM-56 course.
campus: Udine (sede di Udine), Friuli Venezia Giulia, Italy. Delivered by the Dipartimento di Scienze Economiche e Statistiche (DIES — Department of Economics and Statistics). Not delivered outside Udine (unlike e.g. the LM-77 Banca e Finanza course, whose seat is Pordenone).
degree_class: LM-56 — Scienze dell'economia. Single degree class, not an interclass programme. The Manifesto heading reads "ECONOMICS - SCIENZE ECONOMICHE, CLASSE LM-56 (curricula: Economics; Sustainable Development)".
admission_type: open access ("accesso libero") with a curricular/academic requirements check — no entrance exam, no ranked selection call, no TOLC and no SAT. For applicants holding a foreign qualification, an additional mandatory online pre-evaluation ("pre-evaluation application" / prevalutazione) via the Elix-Forms platform is required before enrolment; this is an eligibility assessment, not a competitive ranking.
access_type_detail: "Accesso libero" (open access). The UNIUD course page for Economics - Scienze economiche states the access type as "accesso libero". There is NO numero programmato and NO local quota (programmazione locale) for this master's degree: the 2026/27 Economia Manifesto lists the course simply as "Economics - Scienze Economiche, classe LM-56, sede di Udine. Curricula: Economics; Sustainable Development. Corso erogato in inglese. Anni attivati: tutti.", with no place cap — in explicit contrast to the Economics-area BACHELOR courses in the same Manifesto, which are all "Accesso programmato" with stated caps (e.g. Banca e Finanza L-18: 115 places of which 5 reserved for non-EU students resident abroad; Economia Aziendale L-18: 250 places of which 5 non-EU; Economia e Commercio L-33: 200 places of which 15 non-EU; Management & Business Analytics L-18: 100 places of which 30 non-EU). Because the master is accesso libero, admission is not competitive — every applicant meeting the curricular requirements and passing the verification of personal preparation may enrol within the enrolment window.
academic_requirements:
Requirements differ for holders of an Italian degree and holders of a foreign degree (the Manifesto explicitly says: "I requisiti per l'iscrizione sono diversi per studenti in possesso di titolo di laurea italiano e studenti in possesso di titolo di studio conseguito all'estero").

(A) HOLDERS OF AN ITALIAN BACHELOR'S DEGREE — one of the following is required, for BOTH curricula:
• a degree in class L-33 Scienze Economiche or L-18 Scienze dell'economia e della gestione aziendale (ex DM 270/2004), or in class 28 Scienze Economiche or class 17 Scienze dell'economia e della gestione aziendale (ex DM 509/1999); OR
• at least 30 ECTS credits in the scientific-disciplinary sectors SECS-P/01, SECS-P/02, SECS-P/03, SECS-P/05, SECS-P/06, SECS-P/07, SECS-P/08, SECS-P/11, SECS-P/12 AND at least 18 ECTS credits in the sectors SECS-S/01, SECS-S/03, SECS-S/06.
Plus: English language knowledge at level B2 ("livello di conoscenza della lingua inglese B2").
Verification of personal preparation: the knowledge and adequacy of the preparation of ALL students is verified by a dedicated commission of the Course Council ("una apposita commissione del Consiglio di corso di studi"). Candidates who obtained a final bachelor's degree mark of 90/110 or higher are EXEMPT from this verification.

(B) HOLDERS OF A FOREIGN DEGREE (international applicants) — must have completed at least a relevant Bachelor's education, i.e. a bachelor's degree with a major in economics, or in mathematics, engineering (Manifesto wording), and must demonstrate an ability to use English at level B2 or above. The 2026/2027 Additional Notice requirements table is broader and is the operative rule for the Elix-Forms pre-evaluation: "Bachelor degree in Economics or another degree with a focus on Economics or on quantitative subjects such as Accounting, Business, Engineering, Mathematics, Physics, Science, Statistics."
The foreign first-cycle degree must additionally be (a) an official first-cycle degree issued within the relevant foreign education system by an accredited institution, and (b) a degree that gives access, in that system, to equivalent second-cycle courses. Recognition must be documented via a Declaration of Value (Italian Embassy/Consulate) OR CIMEA Statements (cimea-diplome.it); for the 55 Lisbon Recognition Convention signatory countries the ARDI Statement of Correspondence may be downloaded, but the CIMEA Verification Statement is still required.

MINIMUM GPA: none. The 2026/2027 Additional Notice requirements table records "Non applicable." in the Minimum GPA column for the Economics master (the English-language table PDF on the UNIUD site uses the wording "Not indicated."). This is a genuine programme-specific difference: the other four English-taught UNIUD masters carry an explicit minimum (3/4 of the maximum for Industrial Engineering for Sustainable Manufacturing, Management Engineering and AI & Cybersecurity; 60% of the maximum for International Marketing Management & Organization). Note that the 90/110 threshold in (A) is not a minimum admission GPA — it is only an exemption threshold from the preparation-verification interview for Italian-degree holders.
entry_exam_or_test: No entrance exam and no standardised admission test. There is no TOLC (UNIUD's TOLC-E / TOLC-SU requirement applies only to its bachelor courses), no CEnT-S, no SAT and no ranked written test for this master. Two non-competitive assessments exist instead: (1) for Italian-degree holders, a verification of knowledge and adequacy of personal preparation by a dedicated commission of the Course Council, waived at a final bachelor mark of 90/110 or above; (2) for foreign-degree applicants, a documentary evaluation by the Academic Committee within the Elix-Forms pre-evaluation, which "may assess English language skills through an online interview" where no B2-level certificate is provided. For the Economics master an online interview is a possibility, not a fixed step — the 2026/2027 Additional Notice mandates a scheduled online selection interview only for the English-taught BACHELOR (Management and Business Analytics), and names the interview explicitly in the requirement rows of AI & Cybersecurity and International Marketing Management & Organization, not in the Economics row.
entry_test_name_and_deadline: Not applicable — there is no named entry test for this programme, hence no test name, no test registration deadline and no test sitting date. No OFA (obblighi formativi aggiuntivi / additional learning requirements) mechanism applies at master level for this course; the OFA regime described in the 2026/27 Economia Manifesto (with CISIA TOLC-E / TOLC-SU tests and remedial obligations in Mathematics for Business, Microeconomics, Statistics for Business) belongs to the Economics-area BACHELOR programmes only. The only pre-enrolment academic checkpoints and their timing are: (a) the Course Council commission's verification of personal preparation for Italian-degree holders — carried out after application and before/at enrolment, automatically waived at ≥90/110; and (b) for foreign-degree applicants, the Elix-Forms pre-evaluation, which must be submitted within the pre-evaluation window (01/02/2026–31/05/2026 for non-EU residents; 01/02/2026–10/09/2026 for EU residents) and is resolved within 30 working days. Both checkpoints are taken BEFORE enrolment, not after.
reserved_places_non_eu: [uncertain] No programme-specific non-EU quota figure could be verified for the Economics LM-56 master for a.a. 2026/2027 in the retrievable official uniud.it documents. The 2026/2027 Additional Notice (non-EU version) states: "For each degree course, an annual quota of places is reserved for students residing in non-EU countries. The quota for the academic year 2026/2027 can be found in Annex 1 of this Notice." — but Annex 1 for 2026/27 was not published as a separately retrievable file at the time of research (the only annex file reachable on uniud.it is the 2024/25 one, whose URL now returns an editor login page). The 2026/27 Economia Manifesto states non-EU reserved places only for the four ACCESSO PROGRAMMATO bachelor courses of the Economics area and gives no cap or reserved-place figure for the LM-56 master, consistent with its accesso libero status. Practical reading: for an accesso libero master the non-EU contingent functions as an administrative visa-quota figure in Annex 1 rather than a competitive cap, but the exact 2026/27 number for Economics remains unverified — applicants should consult Annex 1 of the 2026/2027 Additional Notice or contact studenti@uniud.it.
admin_seat_university: University of Udine (Università degli Studi di Udine, UNIUD) — sole administering university. This is NOT an inter-university (interateneo), joint or double-degree programme: the 2026/27 Economia Manifesto lists a double degree partner only for the LM-77 International Marketing, Management and Organization course ("Double Degree con Carinthia University of Applied Sciences/CUAS"), and no partner institution is attached to the LM-56 Economics entry. Admission, pre-evaluation (Elix-Forms), enrolment (immatricolazione), tuition/fees and student records are all handled by UNIUD, through the Dipartimento di Scienze Economiche e Statistiche (DIES) at the Udine campus. Contacts: didattica.dies@uniud.it (teaching/preparation assessment), segreteria.economia@uniud.it (Economics student registry), studenti@uniud.it and the Mobility and International Relations Office, Palazzo Garzolini Di Toppo Wassermann, Via Gemona 92, 33100 Udine (international applicants).
course_status_flag: Active and fully offered — NOT "ad esaurimento". The 2026/27 Economia Manifesto degli studi entry reads: "Economics - Scienze Economiche, classe LM-56, sede di Udine. Curricula: Economics; Sustainable Development. Corso erogato in inglese. Anni attivati: tutti." ("Anni attivati: tutti" = all years of the programme are activated, i.e. first-year enrolment is open). By contrast the same Manifesto flags other courses as being phased out — e.g. "(Economia Aziendale, classe LM-77, Ordinamento 2025, Curriculum Economia e gestione delle Amministrazione pubbliche: attivato secondo anno ad esaurimento.)" and "(Economia Aziendale, classe L-18, Ordinamento 2010: attivato terzo anno ad esaurimento)". Neither the Economics LM-56 course nor either of its curricula carries such a flag. The course is also listed among the five English-taught masters in the 2026/2027 Additional Notice, confirming it is recruiting for 2026/27.
language_requirements:
ENGLISH — certified knowledge at CEFR level B2 or equivalent is required. Additional Notice 2026/2027: "For admission to a first or second-cycle degree courses taught in ENGLISH, certified knowledge of the English language of B2 level or equivalent is required, according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR). Only certificates obtained within the last 5 years will be considered valid. Certificates must clearly indicate the achieved level." The 2026/27 Economia Manifesto restates it for this course among the Italian-student requirements ("livello di conoscenza della lingua inglese B2") and for international students ("must demonstrate an ability to use English at level B2 or above").

ACCEPTED CERTIFICATES (the recognised list in the 2026/2027 Additional Notice): Cambridge English Language Assessment; Trinity College London; IELTS – International English Language Testing System; TOEFL – Test of English as a Foreign Language; Pearson Edexcel – Test of English Academic (PTE Academic); Pearson General English; Oxford Test of English; LanguageCert International ESOL; Gatehouse Awards Classic; British Council – Aptis ESOL General; British Council – Aptis ESOL Advanced.

EXEMPTIONS: "Prospective students are exempt from providing a B2-level English language certification if they have completed a school programme taught in English (IB diplomas, multilingual schools, etc.) or if they are native English speakers" (the Notice links https://www.gov.uk/english-language/exemptions for the list of native-English countries).

ALTERNATIVE ASSESSMENT: "In case of absence of a B2-level or equivalent English language proficiency certificate, the competent Academic Committee may assess English language skills through an online interview."

TIMING FLEXIBILITY: the certificate may be submitted after the pre-evaluation — "It is possible to submit the pre-evaluation application even without the required language certification, provided that the candidate is awaiting the English language test or the issuance of the certification. Obtaining the required language certification remains a necessary requirement for completing the enrolment process."

ITALIAN LANGUAGE: not required for this programme. Certified Italian at B2 (CLIQ-issued CELI / CILS / CERTIT / PLIDA) is required only for degree courses taught in Italian, or in both Italian and English at B2 for partially English-taught courses — neither case applies here, since Economics is taught entirely in English. Non-EU-resident visa applicants must nevertheless attach to their Universitaly pre-enrolment a "certificate of English language proficiency of B2 level or equivalent if applying for a degree course taught in English".
english_level_exception: No programme-specific exception applies to Economics — the standard UNIUD requirement of B2 applies in full. The only English-level exception at UNIUD is for a different programme: "For the Master's degree course in Management Engineering, the required level of English language proficiency is B1." The same paragraph adds: "For degree courses taught partially in English, the required level of proficiency in both Italian and English remains B2 or equivalent" — also not applicable here, as Economics is fully English-taught. Practical consequence: an applicant to Economics needs a genuine B2, whereas the same applicant would clear Management Engineering at B1.
english_cert_validity_years: 5 years. General UNIUD rule for 2026/2027, applying to this programme with no deviation: "Only certificates obtained within the last 5 years will be considered valid. Certificates must clearly indicate the achieved level." The rule appears identically in both the EU-resident and non-EU-resident versions of the 2026/2027 Additional Notice. Note the practical trap: a certificate issued more than 5 years before application is rejected even if the issuing body treats it as lifetime-valid (e.g. Cambridge certificates) — an applicant in that position falls back on the Academic Committee's online English interview or on an exemption (English-medium schooling / native speaker).
teaching_language_partial_flag: fully English (100%) — not partial, and not a case of an English track alongside an Italian track. Both curricula of the programme, "Economics" and "Sustainable Development", are delivered in English: "Gli insegnamenti di entrambi i curricula sono erogati in lingua inglese." There is therefore no Italian-taught branch of this LM-56 course and no ECTS-based partial-English caveat; the whole 120 ECTS is delivered in English. Consequently the "partially in English" rule of the Additional Notice (which would require B2 in BOTH Italian and English) does not apply, and no Italian language certificate is required.
application_deadline_eu: 01/02/2026 – 10/09/2026 (Elix-Forms online pre-evaluation window for applicants RESIDING IN EU COUNTRIES who hold a qualification obtained abroad). Additional Notice 2026/2027 (EU version): "Applications for admission to master's degree courses taught in Italian and in English must be submitted on the Elix-Forms platform between 01/02/2026 and 10/09/2026." Note that EU residents holding an ITALIAN bachelor's degree do not use Elix-Forms at all — they apply directly through the ordinary immatricolazione procedure within the enrolment window (9 July – 5 October 2026). The 10/09/2026 pre-evaluation deadline sits deliberately just before the 5 October enrolment cut-off, but leaves only about three weeks of margin once the 30-working-day decision period is counted, so applying near the deadline is risky.
application_deadline_non_eu: 01/02/2026 – 31/05/2026 (Elix-Forms online pre-evaluation window for applicants RESIDING IN NON-EU COUNTRIES). Additional Notice 2026/2027 (non-EU version): "Applications for admission to Master's degree courses taught in Italian or English must be submitted through the Elix-Forms platform between 01/02/2026 and 31/05/2026." This closes 3.5 months earlier than the EU window because the resulting Letter of Eligibility must feed the Universitaly pre-enrolment and study-visa procedure. The 31/05/2026 deadline and the separate 30/06/2026 Universitaly deadline are cumulative, not alternative: a non-EU applicant must clear both.
universitaly_deadline: 30 June 2026 — Universitaly pre-enrolment (visa) deadline, applying ONLY to applicants residing in non-EU countries who need a study visa. Additional Notice 2026/2027: prospective students "MUST create their digital profile on the UNIVERSITALY portal ... and submitting the digital PRE-ENROLMENT application for a degree course at the University of Udine for the academic year 2026/2027 by the 30th of June 2026 at the latest. Pre-enrolment applications submitted after the 30th of June 2026 will not be considered." This is a DIFFERENT and LATER deadline than the UNIUD Elix-Forms pre-evaluation deadline of 31/05/2026 — the two must not be conflated; the Elix-Forms application comes first and produces the Letter of Eligibility that the Universitaly pre-enrolment relies on. Documents to attach on Universitaly: valid passport; passport-sized photograph; first-cycle university degree (or final/provisional single-cycle master's degree) for second-cycle applicants; certificate of English language proficiency at B2 level or equivalent (the programme being English-taught). Binding consequences: "Applicants requesting a study visa for Italy may complete their enrolment at the University of Udine only for the degree course chosen on the Universitaly portal" and "Changing degree course after arriving at the University of Udine, as well as transferring to other Italian universities during the first year of enrolment, is not permitted." Pre-enrolment does not guarantee a consular appointment, and preliminary acceptance by UNIUD confers no right to a visa.
decision_timeline_days: 30 working days from submission of the complete pre-evaluation application. Additional Notice 2026/2027 (both EU and non-EU versions, master's degree section): "After submitting the pre-evaluation application with all required documentation and the paid fee, the application will be forwarded for the evaluation to the Academic Committee, which will communicate the outcome of the assessment to the applicant via email within 30 working days from the date of submission." The clock starts only for COMPLETE applications — "only complete applications will be evaluated, meaning the applications for which the required fee has been duly paid." A positive outcome produces an emailed Letter of Eligibility for Enrolment; for non-EU-resident applicants this then triggers the invitation to apply for a study visa via Universitaly, while EU-resident applicants are simply invited to proceed with the further enrolment steps.
enrolment_window: 9 July 2026 – 5 October 2026 at 12:00 noon, for immatricolazione to master's degree courses. 2026/27 Economia Manifesto: "Le domande d'immatricolazione ai corsi di laurea magistrale si presentano dal 9 luglio al 5 ottobre 2026 alle ore 12.00, con proroga che può essere concessa dal Rettore, per giustificati motivi, fino alle ore 12.00 del 15 gennaio 2027" — i.e. the Rector may grant an extension to 15 January 2027, 12:00, on submission of a late-enrolment request bearing a €16.00 stamp duty (marca da bollo). No late-request instrument is needed for students who obtained their bachelor's degree after 5 October 2026. Students graduating in the extraordinary session (after 15 January 2027) may instead enrol in single courses (corsi singoli) and later obtain career abbreviation with validation of exams passed. NO chronological-order / places-exhaustion warning applies to this course: the "domande di immatricolazione sono accettate in ordine cronologico e fino ad esaurimento dei posti" rule and the associated waiting-list mechanism in the Manifesto govern the accesso programmato BACHELOR courses, not this accesso libero master. Before enrolling online, applicants must self-certify their qualifications, listing exams passed, marks and the scientific-disciplinary sector (SSD) of each course so that the curricular requirements can be verified; the University reserves the right to verify access qualifications and to exclude or annul the enrolment of anyone found not to meet them at any time. Fee-reduction requests must be filed by 5 October 2026.
tuition_or_fees_link: https://www.uniud.it/it/didattica/area-servizi-studenti/servizi-studenti/diritto-allo-studio/tasse_merito — the official UNIUD tuition/fees and right-to-study page, cited by the 2026/27 Economia Manifesto ("Avviso aggiuntivo al Manifesto degli studi per l'anno accademico 2026/27 relativo a tasse, contributi ed esoneri reperibile alla pagina ..."). The Avviso aggiuntivo on fees, contributions and exemptions is an integral part of the Manifesto degli studi. Fee-reduction requests are due by 5 October 2026. uncertainty_notes:
1) RESERVED NON-EU PLACES (reserved_places_non_eu) — the only genuinely unresolved field. The 2026/2027 Additional Notice asserts that a per-course non-EU quota exists and points to "Annex 1 of this Notice", but Annex 1 for 2026/27 is not published as a separately retrievable document on uniud.it; the only annex file indexed (the 2024/25 "Allegato n. 1 al Manifesto — contingente extra UE") now resolves to an editor login page rather than the PDF. The 2026/27 Economia Manifesto states non-EU reserved-place counts only for the accesso programmato bachelor courses of the Economics area and none for the LM-56 master, which is consistent with its open-access status. The figure must be confirmed against Annex 1 or with studenti@uniud.it before being published to applicants.

2) EU vs. NON-EU DEADLINE ASYMMETRY — the two pre-evaluation windows share the same opening date (01/02/2026) but differ in closing date (10/09/2026 for EU residents vs 31/05/2026 for non-EU residents). The relevant criterion in both notices is COUNTRY OF RESIDENCE, not citizenship: a non-EU citizen legally resident in an EU country falls under the EU-resident notice and the later 10/09/2026 deadline. This distinction is a frequent source of applicant error and should be surfaced explicitly in any front-end presentation.

3) THREE DISTINCT DEADLINES MUST NOT BE CONFLATED for non-EU-resident applicants: Elix-Forms pre-evaluation by 31/05/2026, Universitaly pre-enrolment by 30/06/2026, and immatricolazione from 09/07/2026 to 05/10/2026 (Rectoral extension to 15/01/2027). All three are cumulative.

4) TWO PARALLEL ADMISSION TRACKS — the Manifesto requirements for holders of an ITALIAN bachelor's degree (L-33/L-18 classes, or 30 ECTS in SECS-P sectors + 18 ECTS in SECS-S sectors) are markedly narrower and more formalised than the requirements applied to holders of a FOREIGN degree via Elix-Forms ("Economics or another degree with a focus on Economics or on quantitative subjects such as Accounting, Business, Engineering, Mathematics, Physics, Science, Statistics"). International applicants are assessed under the latter, broader standard by the Academic Committee, so an engineering, mathematics or physics background is explicitly admissible for them. The SECS-P/SECS-S ECTS thresholds should NOT be presented to international applicants as hard requirements.

5) MINOR SOURCE DIVERGENCE, NOT MATERIAL — the standalone English requirements-table PDF renders the Economics Minimum GPA cell as "Not indicated.", whereas the 2026/2027 Additional Notice renders the same cell as "Non applicable." Both mean that no minimum GPA is enforced for this programme; the Additional Notice is the governing document. Separately, the 90/110 figure in the Italian-degree track is an exemption threshold from the preparation-verification interview, not an admission GPA floor, and applies only to Italian-degree holders.

6) ONLINE INTERVIEW STATUS — for Economics the online interview is discretionary (triggered mainly by a missing English certificate, or by the Academic Committee's assessment of a borderline academic profile) rather than a scheduled step. The 2026/2027 Additional Notice prescribes a scheduled online selection interview only for the English-taught bachelor (Management and Business Analytics), and names the interview inside the requirement rows of AI & Cybersecurity and International Marketing Management & Organization — not inside the Economics row.

7) NOT AN INTERATENEO / JOINT PROGRAMME — unlike some UNIUD courses (e.g. the Udine–Trieste inter-university healthcare degrees, or the LM-77 International Marketing, Management and Organization double degree with Carinthia University of Applied Sciences), this LM-56 course is administered solely by the University of Udine, with no partner institution and no split administrative seat.

8) TUITION AMOUNTS NOT CAPTURED — per the agreed field scope, tuition brackets, ISEE-based reductions and exemptions were not researched as a structured field; only the official fees page link is recorded. The one fee figure verified is the €20.00 non-refundable Elix-Forms pre-evaluation fee (PagoPA), plus the €16.00 stamp duty attached to a late-enrolment request. Application platform for foreign-qualification holders is Elix-Forms (entry point for Economics reachable from the "Degrees taught entirely in English" page, https://goto.uniud.it/to/619).
